newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends poised at 70 cts ahead of RB statement.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends poised at 70 cts ahead of RB statement.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed near its session lows having traded on light flows in a market poised for Tuesday's key Reserve Bank Monetary Policy statement.
The Kiwi closed at 0.US$0.6998/05 compared with its 0.7015/20 opening while the Trade-Weighted Index ended at 66.79 slightly below its 67.01 opening.
The market is mostly square and quietly awaiting the MPS at 9.00 a.m. (2000 GMT). Shorts were generally squeezed out last week when the kiwi headed back up over 70 cents from an earlier dip.
Much interest will focus on what Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash has to say rather than the MPS itself which was finalised before the coalition government was announced last week.
"The market will look to digest how Brash sees the new government and its policies," said a Wellington dealer. Brash will hold a news conference as well as releasing the MPS.
The dealer said he expects Brash to sanction the recent easing of conditions without altering the bank's assumptions about the currency and interest rates.
Another dealer agreed, saying he would be very surprised if Brash sanctioned any further easing than had already occurred.

The second dealer said the bank may again call for a change in the mix of conditions -- asking for a lower exchange rate and relatively higher interest rates. "But we will be recommending to our clients to buy the dips, because nothing will have really changed," he said.
